sec: Overview of hormones: structure-based classification · p830

items.q: Match each hormone to its structure class — 1) T3/T4  2) Serotonin  3) Insulin  4) Aldosterone … A) Tryptophan derivative  B) Steroid hormone  C) Tyrosine derivative  D) Large peptide
items.exp: Tyrosine derivatives are T3/T4 and catecholamines; serotonin and melatonin are tryptophan derivatives; insulin is a large peptide; aldosterone is a steroid. (Book p830)

items.q: All of the following are catecholamines of the adrenal medulla EXCEPT:
items.exp: Catecholamines (adrenal medulla) are adrenaline (80%), noradrenaline and dopamine; melatonin is a tryptophan derivative. (Book p830)

items.q: Adrenaline forms what percentage of adrenal medulla catecholamines?
items.exp: Adrenaline is 80% of the catecholamines of the adrenal medulla. (Book p830)

items.q: Growth hormone is a large peptide of ___ amino acids.
items.exp: Growth hormone has 191 amino acids (prolactin 199, insulin 51). (Book p830)

items.q: Prolactin is a large peptide of ___ amino acids.
items.exp: Prolactin has 199 amino acids (growth hormone 191, insulin 51). (Book p830)

items.q: The number of amino acids in insulin is:
items.exp: Insulin has 51 amino acids and is grouped under large peptides (>50 AA). (Book p830)

items.q: Which of the following is classed as a SMALL peptide (<50 amino acids)?
items.exp: Small peptides (<50 AA) include ACTH, ADH, oxytocin and all hypothalamic hormones; GH, prolactin, insulin, PTH and renin are large peptides. (Book p830)

items.q: ‘Glycoprotein hormones (FSH, LH, TSH) contain more carbohydrate than protein.’
items.exp: Glycoproteins are defined as protein > carbohydrate; FSH/LH/TSH are >200 AA with a common α subunit. (Book p830)

items.q: FSH, LH and TSH share which structural feature?
opts: A common α subunit and >200 amino acids
A common β subunit and 51 amino acids
items.exp: The glycoproteins FSH, LH and TSH are >200 AA and share a common α subunit. (Book p830)

items.q: Match the adrenal cortex zone to its hormone — 1) Zona glomerulosa  2) Zona fasciculata  3) Zona reticularis … A) Cortisol  B) Aldosterone  C) Androgens (DHEAS/androstenedione)
items.exp: Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone; zona fasciculata → cortisol; zona reticularis → adrenal androgens (DHEAS, androstenedione). (Book p830)

items.q: DHEAS is described as the most abundant adreno-cortical hormone during:
items.exp: Note: DHEAS (dihydroepiandrosterone sulfate) is the most abundant adreno-cortical hormone in fetal life. (Book p830)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the sex hormones listed?
items.exp: Sex hormones are estrogen, progesterone and testosterone; cortisol is an adrenal cortex (fasciculata) steroid. (Book p830)
Vitamin derivatives in the classification are vitamin A and vitamin D. (Book p830)
